proposals.observation: The Daily Blog Post workflow failed at 06:04 UTC on 22 July. The content queue shows only 1 post queued against 47 published, meaning the pipeline is not refilling the queue. With the workflow broken, Joel's organic content output drops to zero until this is fixed. Blog posts are the top-of-funnel asset for the 25-35 ICP, and two consecutive workflow failures (blog + digest) suggest a shared dependency — possibly an expired API token, a changed secret name, or a broken package step introduced outside the protected files.
proposals.proposal: Inspect the Daily Blog Post workflow run logs for the failure at 2026-07-22T06:04:29Z. The most probable causes, given only a cursor-state commit landed in the last 24 hours, are: an expired OPENAI_API_KEY or MAILERLITE_API_KEY secret, a missing environment variable after a recent secret rotation, or a `npm ci` step failing because package-lock.json drifted (the file is protected from Fred edits, so any manual change to it would not show in Fred's commits). Check the step-level failure message in the Actions tab, then either rotate the relevant secret or re-pin the failing step's Node version. Because `.github/workflows/*` is in the blocked-paths list, Joel must make this fix manually — Fred is flagging it so it does not sit another 24 hours.

proposals.observation: The Funnel-Hack Digest workflow also failed on the same day (10:51 UTC), a few hours after the blog post failure. Two separate named workflows failing within 5 hours, with no code changes in between beyond a cursor update, points to a shared infrastructure cause rather than logic errors in either workflow individually. If both workflows call the same secret or the same external API, fixing the root cause once should restore both. The digest failure also means Joel has no fresh competitive or content intelligence coming in, which compounds the content-queue drought identified in Observation 1.
proposals.proposal: After fixing the root cause identified in Proposal 1, trigger a manual re-run of the Funnel-Hack Digest workflow from the Actions tab (select the failed run, click "Re-run all jobs"). Do not edit the workflow file itself unless the step logs show a logic error specific to the digest. If re-running after the secret fix still fails, check whether the digest workflow calls a different third-party endpoint (e.g. an RSS scraper or a separate API) that may have its own expired credential. Document the fix in a plain-text ops note so the pattern is visible next time two workflows fail on the same morning.

proposals.impact: reduces zero-start drop-off on quiz intro screen
proposals.observation: The quiz had 1 session in the last 48 hours, 0 starts, and 0 completions. The sole visitor loaded the intro screen and left without pressing start. This is a 0% conversion at the very first interaction point. Even accounting for low traffic, a single visitor who sees the intro and bounces tells us the intro screen is not earning the click. The current data cannot tell us whether the copy is the problem or the traffic is cold, but since the intro screen is the one thing Fred can edit today, improving it costs nothing and removes a known friction point before more traffic arrives.
proposals.proposal: Rewrite the quiz intro headline and subhead to be specific to the felt experience of the ICP rather than describing the quiz as a quiz. The current text (reproduced below) leads with a category label. Replace it with a sentence that names the specific tension a 28-year-old earning £60k but saving nothing actually feels on a Tuesday morning, grounded in Joel's own story where relevant. The new text passes the Sultanic test because no other coach has the gym-bag moment or the unopened tax-return tab.
